subject: Spectra RFP: key custody, rotation windows, and TLS profile
messages:

Subject: Spectra RFP: initial questions on key custody and rotation

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intros last week. Our procurement and security teams are working through the encryption and key management section of the RFP and had a few clarifying questions before we complete scoring. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) BYOK options: do you support both customer-imported symmetric keys and vault-backed keys with HSM attestations? Which HSM vendors are supported for on-prem BYOK integrations?

2) Key rotation: what are the options for rotation cadence (customer-controlled vs. Redwood-managed), and what controls exist to force immediate rotation or emergency key revocation?

3) TLS profile: minimum TLS version and any hard requirements around ciphers / mutual TLS for admin API endpoints.

If you can provide an annotated response and any evidence artifacts (attestation letters, SOC2 AOC, configuration guides) that would be ideal. We have a soft deadline to finalize the security section by EOW next Friday.

Appreciate it — copying procurement (procure@spectra-analytics.com) for visibility.

Regards,
Anna Keller
Director, IT Risk | Spectra Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: procure@spectra-analytics.com
Date: 2026-06-22T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spectra RFP: initial questions on key custody and rotation

Anna — thanks for the clear list. Below is an initial, concise response; I am also looping in Marcus (security lead) and Priyom (solution engineer) to add operational artifacts and a short rotation policy we can include as an appendix.

1) BYOK options:
- Supported: import of customer symmetric keys (wrapped key import), envelope encryption where customer-managed CMK in a supported KMS/HSM wraps data encryption keys (DEKs), and direct HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- HSM integrations: we have production integrations and attestations for Thales and AWS CloudHSM; we also support customer-managed HSMs via standard PKCS#11 interfaces in Private deployments.

2) Key rotation and revocation:
- Modes: a) Customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) — customer controls rotation cadence & lifecycle; b) Redwood-managed keys — we rotate DEKs automatically and rotate wrapping keys per internal policy (90 days default), with emergency-rekey procedures.
- Emergency actions: immediate key revocation (blacklist) at the routing layer; we support re-encryption of stored objects using a new wrapping key as a remediation path. For BYOK, revocation is controlled by the customer (we will stop encrypting with a key once instructed).

3) TLS profile:
- Minimum TLS 1.2 for data plane; we recommend TLS 1.3 where clients support it. Admin/control plane APIs in Private deployments can be configured to require mutual TLS (mTLS).
- Cipher guidance: recommend ECDHE ciphers with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 (e.g., TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256). We can provide a hardening checklist if needed.

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_RFI-answers_v1.pdf (initial write-up). I will follow up with SOC2 AOC and HSM attestation artifacts.

Next steps: Marcus / Priyom — can you add the SOC attestation and the operational excerpt on rotation windows + sample API calls for key injection? Happy to send a consolidated packet to Spectra once we have those.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Kim / Priyom — forwarding Anna's note and Kimberly's reply. Quick suggestions from security for the packet before we send to Spectra:

- Include SOC2 AOC (2025) and an HSM attestation letter from our Thales partner. Those are commonly requested and reduce back-and-forth.
- Add an operational excerpt that explains: key import flow, wrapping/unwrapping steps, who has access (roles & MFA gating), and audit log examples (sample JSON entries). Don't expose internal IPs — provide sanitized logs.
- Clarify rotation capabilities: we should call out minimum supported rotation granularity (hourly for ephemeral session keys, daily for DEKs on request, monthly default for wrapping keys unless customer overrides). Also specify re-encryption SLA if we need to rewrap stored objects after key replacement (e.g., background job completes within 72 hours for up to 50TB in Dedicated configurations; larger volumes negotiated).

I can attach SOC2-AOC-2025.pdf and a zipped attestation package (HSM_Attestation_Thales.zip). Priyom, can you prepare the sample API snippets and the compact diagram for key flows?

-Marcus

Thanks — attached are the artifacts I'm proposing to include (I put the API snippets and a short operational policies extract into the drive link below). Highlights to include in the final packet:

- BYOK modes: import via PKCS#7-wrapped symmetric keys (import API), CMK provisioning via customer KMS (BYOK via external KMS connector), and full HSM-backed key control for Private/Dedicated.

- Rotation policy (concise language for RFP):
  * Customer-managed CMKs: rotation cadence controlled by customer; Redwood will honor key lifecycle state (active, disabled, destroyed) as provided by the customer's KMS or HSM attestation.
  * Redwood-managed wrapping keys (hosted): default rotation every 90 days; customer may opt for 30/60/90-day cadence.
  * DEKs: automatically rotated per workload; support for ephemeral (per-request) DEKs for high-security routes.
  * Emergency revocation: immediate disablement, plus a documented re-encryption remediation plan.

- TLS: we recommend TLS 1.3 when possible. Admin/control-plane endpoints support mTLS; data-plane endpoints support TLS 1.2+ and will retire weak ciphers on vendor timeline.

- Evidence bundle: SOC2-AOC-2025.pdf, HSM_Attestation_Thales.zip (contains vendor attestation and code-signed firmware checks), and a short README describing redaction rules for logs.

Drive packet: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD-example

If that's good, I'll assemble the final PDF and Kimberly can send to Spectra. Priyom

Anna — thanks for your patience. Attached is a consolidated packet addressing the RFP questions you raised: a concise written response, SOC2 AOC, HSM attestation materials, and a short operational excerpt describing rotation and emergency procedures. A few key points up front:

- BYOK & HSM: Redwood supports both customer-imported keys (wrapped key import) and external/customer HSMs via PKCS#11 in Private deployments. We maintain production attestations with Thales and support AWS CloudHSM for cloud-based customer keys.
- Rotation & revocation: customers may manage CMK rotation schedules via their KMS/HSM. For Redwood-managed wrapping keys we offer configurable rotation cadence (30/60/90 days) with a 90-day default; DEKs are rotated automatically and ephemeral keys are available for high-security routes. Emergency revocation is supported and we document the re-encryption path; rewrap jobs complete within 72 hours for typical Dedicated volumes (detailed SLA negotiable).
- TLS & hardening: data plane requires TLS 1.2+; we recommend TLS 1.3. Admin/control plane can be configured for mTLS. Cipher recommendations are included in the attached hardening checklist.
